series.name: Galaxy S
historical_notes: First released in 2010 as Samsung's flagship Android smartphone lineup.
Introduced major innovations like Super AMOLED displays and curved screens.
The S series is Samsung's longest-running and most popular smartphone series.

series.name: Galaxy Note
historical_notes: Introduced in 2011, popularizing the 'phablet' category.
Known for the S Pen stylus and large displays.
Discontinued after 2020 with the Note 20 series, with features merging into the S Ultra series.

series.name: Galaxy Z Fold
historical_notes: First launched in 2019 as Samsung's first foldable smartphone.
Rebranded to Galaxy Z Fold starting with the second generation.
Pioneered the foldable smartphone category.

series.name: Galaxy Z Flip
historical_notes: Launched in 2020 as Samsung's clamshell foldable phone.
Part of the Galaxy Z series, known for its compact, fashionable design.

series.name: Galaxy A
historical_notes: Introduced in 2014 as a mid-range series with a metal build.
Expanded to cover a wide range of price points from entry-level to upper mid-range.
Absorbed the Galaxy J series in 2019.

series.name: Galaxy M
historical_notes: Launched in 2019 as an online-exclusive series.
Replaced the Galaxy J and On series in some markets.
Focused on providing high battery capacity and good specs at a low price.

series.name: Galaxy J
historical_notes: Launched in 2015 as a budget-friendly series.
Merged into the Galaxy A series in 2019.

series.name: Galaxy C
historical_notes: Launched in 2016 exclusively for the Chinese market.
Designed to compete with local Chinese brands.
Discontinued after a short run.

series.name: Galaxy E
historical_notes: Launched in 2015 as an affordable mid-range series.
Short-lived, replaced by the Galaxy A and J series.

series.name: Galaxy F
historical_notes: Launched in 2020 as an online-exclusive series for India and other Asian markets.
Similar to the Galaxy M series but with different marketing.

series.name: Galaxy Grand
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 as a mid-range phablet.
Replaced by the Galaxy E and J series.

series.name: Galaxy Mega
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 with extremely large screens (5.8 and 6.3 inches).
Short-lived, replaced by the Galaxy Note and A series.

series.name: Galaxy R
historical_notes: Launched in 2011 as a high-end variant of the Galaxy S II with an NVIDIA Tegra processor.
Short-lived, only one model released.

series.name: Galaxy W
historical_notes: Originally launched in 2011 as a mid-range device.
Rebranded as a premium clamshell (flip) phone series exclusively for the Chinese market.
Known as the 'Heart of the World' series in China.

series.name: Galaxy XCover
historical_notes: First rugged smartphone series from Samsung.
Originally launched in 2011, with the XCover Pro and XCover 6 Pro being notable business-focused models.
The series is known for its durability and enterprise features.

series.name: Galaxy Pocket
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 as an entry-level smartphone with a very small screen.
Replaced by the Galaxy J and A series.

series.name: Galaxy Young
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as an entry-level smartphone for young users.
Short-lived, only one model released.

series.name: Galaxy Star
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as one of Samsung's cheapest smartphones.
Short-lived.

series.name: Galaxy Ace
historical_notes: Launched in 2011 as a popular budget-friendly smartphone.
Replaced by the Galaxy J and A series.

series.name: Galaxy Core
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as a budget-friendly dual-SIM smartphone.
Replaced by the Galaxy J and A series.

series.name: Galaxy Express
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as a mid-range smartphone with 4G LTE support.
Short-lived.

series.name: Galaxy Feel
historical_notes: Launched in 2017 exclusively for the Japanese market.
Sold through NTT Docomo.

series.name: Galaxy Golden
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as a premium clamshell phone with dual displays.
Primarily sold in South Korea and China.

series.name: Galaxy Folder
historical_notes: Launched in 2015 as a smartphone with a clamshell form factor.

series.name: Galaxy Win
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as a mid-range dual-SIM smartphone.
Known as Galaxy Grand Quattro in some markets.

series.name: Galaxy Fame
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as an entry-level smartphone.
Short-lived.

series.name: Galaxy Trend

Short-lived.

series.name: Galaxy Music

series.name: Galaxy Discover

series.name: Galaxy Indulge

series.name: Galaxy Reverb

series.name: Galaxy Rush

series.name: Galaxy Stellar

series.name: Galaxy Admire
historical_notes: Launched in 2011 for MetroPCS.
Mid-range Android smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy Appeal
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 for AT&T.
Budget-friendly smartphone with a physical keyboard.

series.name: Galaxy Attain
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 for MetroPCS.
Mid-range 4G LTE smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy Axiom

Mid-range 4G LTE smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy Centura
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 for Straight Talk.
Budget-friendly smartphone with stock Android.

series.name: Galaxy Exhibit

series.name: Galaxy Prevail

series.name: Galaxy Proclaim
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 for Straight Talk.
Budget-friendly Android smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy Repp
historical_notes: Launched in 2011 for U.S. Cellular.
Budget-friendly Android smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy Round

Exclusive to SK Telecom in South Korea.

series.name: Galaxy S Duos
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 as a dual-SIM variant of the Galaxy S series.
Part of the Galaxy S family but with dual-SIM functionality.

series.name: Galaxy S Plus

series.name: Galaxy Victory

series.name: Galaxy V

series.name: Galaxy Y
historical_notes: Launched in 2011 as an entry-level smartphone.

series.name: Galaxy S Vibrant
historical_notes: Launched in 2010 for T-Mobile USA as a variant of the Galaxy S.
Part of the original Galaxy S lineup.

series.name: Galaxy X
historical_notes: An experimental foldable smartphone prototype that never saw a commercial release.
Rumored and trademarked but not officially sold.

series.name: Galaxy Z
historical_notes: The Galaxy Z series encompasses both the Fold and Flip lines.
Introduced in 2020 with the Galaxy Z Flip and Z Fold2.
Represents Samsung's flagship foldable smartphones.

series.name: Galaxy On
historical_notes: Launched in 2015 as an online-exclusive series for emerging markets.
Replaced by the Galaxy M and F series.

series.name: Galaxy K
historical_notes: Launched in 2014 as a camera-centric smartphone with an optical zoom lens.
Replaced by the Galaxy S Zoom series.

series.name: Galaxy S Zoom
historical_notes: Launched in 2013 as a camera-focused smartphone with a 10x optical zoom.

series.name: Galaxy Beam
historical_notes: Launched in 2012 with a built-in pico projector.

series.name: Galaxy Mini

series.name: Galaxy Pocket Neo

series.name: Galaxy Fame Lite

series.name: Galaxy Star 2

Short-lived.

series.name: Galaxy Young 2

Short-lived.

naming_strategy.description: Samsung uses a combination of letters (S, A, M, etc.) and numbers to denote different market segments and generations. The 'Galaxy' prefix is used for all smartphones. Flagship models use the 'S' and 'Note' series, while mid-range and budget models use 'A', 'M', 'J', etc. Foldable phones are under the 'Z' series. Various suffixes like 'Lite', 'Plus', 'Ultra', and 'FE' indicate different variants within a series.

summary.future_expected_direction: Continued focus on foldables (Galaxy Z series), AI integration across all series, and expanding the mid-range A and M series with 5G and improved cameras.
